title: Abstract Nouns & Classical Proper Names
source: Original instructional lesson authored for this application (syllabus ref: Haywood & Nahmad Ch. 41; Ryding Ch. 5)
objectives: Form abstract nouns (al-maṣdar al-ṣināʿī) with the suffix ـِيَّةٌ (e.g., إِنْسَانِيَّةٌ, عِلْمِيَّةٌ).
Identify the four components of classical Arabic names: ism, kunya, nasab, and laqab.
Parse patronymic chains using ابْنُ / بِنْتُ (dropping initial alif of ابْنُ between two proper names).
recallPrompt: From Chapter 40: How does the nisbah suffix ـِيٌّ attach to a noun?

sections.heading: Abstract Nouns & Classical Biographical Names
sections.body: Adding ـِيَّةٌ (feminine nisbah ending) to a noun or adjective creates an abstract noun (e.g., حُرٌّ 'free' → حُرِّيَّةٌ 'freedom'). In classical literature and history, personal names follow a structured four-part system: given name (ism), teknonym (kunya: Abū / Umm), lineage (nasab: ibn / bint), and honorific epithet (laqab).

sections.label: Orthography of اِبْنُ Between Two Names
sections.summary: When ابْنُ ('son of') stands directly between a person's name and their father's name (on the same line), its initial alif is dropped in writing: عُمَرُ بْنُ الخَطَّابِ (ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb).

sections.arabic: أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ إِسْمَاعِيلَ البُخَارِيُّ
sections.transliteration: ʾabū ʿabdi llāhi muḥammadu bnu ʾismāʿīla l-bukhāriyyu
sections.translation: Abū ʿAbd Allāh Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl al-Bukhārī.
sections.irab: أَبُو: كُنْيَةٌ مَرْفُوعٌ بِالوَاوِ | مُحَمَّدُ: اِسْمٌ (بَدَلٌ) مَرْفُوعٌ | بْنُ: نَعْتٌ/بَدَلٌ مُضَافٌ | إِسْمَاعِيلَ: مُضَافٌ إِلَيْهِ مَجْرُورٌ بِالفَتْحَةِ (مَمْنُوعٌ مِنَ الصَّرْفِ) | البُخَارِيُّ: نِسْبَةٌ
sections.notes: Notice how a single classical citation combines kunya (أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ), ism (مُحَمَّدُ), nasab (بْنُ إِسْمَاعِيلَ), and nisbah (البُخَارِيُّ).

sections.heading: Case Inflection of أَبُو (The Five Nouns)
sections.body: أَبٌ ('father') and أَخٌ ('brother') inflect with long letters when annexed: أَبُو (nom.), أَبَا (acc.), أَبِي (gen.).
